text:
Marathon Petroleum stock dropped 0.82% today to close at $370.78, extending a sharp five-day decline of roughly 11%. The sell-off appears linked to escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran has launched direct attacks on U.S. military installations in the Gulf region, including Kuwait, and the IEA warned that the Iran conflict has "crushed" confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor. While oil prices remain firm at nearly $90 per barrel domestically, this geopolitical risk and supply-route uncertainty have rattled energy stocks, and refinery margins (the profit refiners make by processing crude into products) are likely under pressure as markets price in potential disruption.

The broader context adds weight to the sell-off: U.S. refineries are already running at a high utilization rate of 95.7%, leaving little room to boost output if supply routes tighten, and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain relatively low. When refiners are already running flat-out and can't easily scale up production in response to supply shocks, their margins compress—refiners earn less per barrel processed. The geopolitical overhang matters more when there's no spare capacity to absorb it.
